Wind speed at the blending height

Source: R/metric-aerodynamics.R
ef_blending_wind.Rd

Extrapolates the wind speed measured at a weather station to the blending height \(z_b\) with the neutral logarithmic wind profile over the surface around the station. METRIC assumes that the wind at the blending height is approximately uniform over the scene; a spatial wind surface is also accepted (vectors per pixel).

Usage

ef_blending_wind(
  wind_speed,
  height,
  zom_station,
  d_station,
  blending_height = 200
)

Arguments

wind_speed

Numeric. Wind speed measured at height [m s-1]. Must be finite and >= 0.

height

Numeric. Measurement height \(z_x\) [m]. Must be finite and greater than d_station + zom_station.

zom_station

Numeric. Momentum roughness length of the surface around the station \(z_{om,w}\) [m]. Must be finite and > 0. No default: METRIC implementations use 0.015 m (clipped grass 0.12 m tall), FAO-56 box 4 gives 0.123 h = 0.01476 m for the same grass (see ef_zom_height()); decision SH-04 is open.

d_station

Numeric. Zero-plane displacement of the station surface \(d_w\) [m]. Must be finite and >= 0. No default: METRIC implementations use 0, FAO-56 gives 2 h / 3 = 0.08 m for grass 0.12 m tall (SH-04).

blending_height

Numeric. Blending height \(z_b\) [m]. Must be finite and greater than d_station + zom_station. Default 200 m (Waters et al., 2002, p. 26, Eq. 29).

Value

A numeric vector of wind speed at the blending height \(u_b\) [m s-1], with the common length of the inputs and keeping their dim.

Details

$$u_b = u_x \frac{\ln\left((z_b - d_w)/z_{om,w}\right)} {\ln\left((z_x - d_w)/z_{om,w}\right)}$$

Assumptions: neutral stability over the station surface and a logarithmic profile up to the blending height. No minimum wind speed is imposed (decision SH-06): low wind is reported, not replaced. No elevation adjustment of the wind is applied (SH-07, not verified).

Missing values propagate. Infinite values and values outside the domain raise an error of class earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error).

Verification status: with \(d_w = 0\), VERIFICADA (SEBAL-Idaho 2002): Waters et al. (2002), p. 26, Eqs. 27 and 29 (neutral friction velocity at the station and wind at 200 m), which use no displacement for the station surface and estimate its roughness as \(z_{om,w} = 0.12 h\) (Eq. 28; h = 0.3 m at Kimberly). A positive \(d_w\) is an extension of the package (CANDIDATA in METRIC, decision SH-04): with \(d_w\) and \(z_{om,w}\) from FAO-56 box 4, the normalised profile coincides with FAO-56, chapter 3, Eq. 47 (author's calculation).

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

Waters, R., Allen, R., Bastiaanssen, W., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2002). SEBAL: Surface Energy Balance Algorithms for Land. Idaho implementation. Advanced training and users manual (Version 1.0). University of Idaho and Idaho Department of Water Resources.

See also

Other aerodynamics and sensible heat functions: ef_air_density(), ef_calibrate_h(), ef_dt_coef(), ef_h_control(), ef_rah(), ef_sensible_heat(), ef_ts_datum(), ef_ustar(), ef_zom()

Examples

# 3 m s-1 at 2 m over grass (z_om,w = 0.015 m, d_w = 0), z_b = 200 m
ef_blending_wind(3, height = 2, zom_station = 0.015, d_station = 0)
#> [1] 5.823611

# Same grass with the FAO-56 displacement and roughness (h = 0.12 m)
ef_blending_wind(3, height = 2, zom_station = 0.01476, d_station = 0.08,
                 blending_height = 200)
#> [1] 5.862843
